did_you_know.text: Did you know? After King Ahasuerus’s anger subsided, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and the punishment decreed against her.
Did you know? At the king’s officials’ suggestion, young women from every province of the kingdom were gathered at the citadel of Susa, brought to the women’s quarters, and provided with cosmetics.
Did you know? Mordecai is described as a Jewish man who lived in the citadel of Susa. He belonged to the family of Kish and the tribe of Benjamin—“a Benjaminite.”
Did you know? Esther was also called Hadassah. She was Mordecai’s cousin, and after her father and mother died, he adopted her as his daughter.
Did you know? Esther did not reveal her people or her family background, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.
Did you know? The young women underwent twelve months of preparation before it was their turn to go to the king: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and women’s cosmetics.

Did you know? When it was Esther’s turn to go to the king, she asked for nothing for herself. She took only what Hegai, the keeper of the women, suggested. Because of this, she won the favor of everyone who saw her.
Did you know? Ahasuerus loved Esther more than any of the other women. He placed the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
Did you know? To celebrate Esther’s coronation, the king held a great banquet, announced tax relief for the provinces, and gave gifts and grants with royal generosity.

Did you know? Mordecai uncovered the plot of Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who guarded the entrance and planned to assassinate Ahasuerus. The matter was investigated, they were hanged, and the incident was recorded in the royal chronicles in the king’s presence.
